blocks.text: Cedar Hills Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Cedar Hills has no City-published neighbourhood boundary. The City of Surrey does not publish Cedar Hills as an official neighbourhood name; the name is anchored on the ground by Cedar Hills Elementary School at 12370 98 Avenue, in the Whalley side of north Surrey near 124 Street and 100 Avenue.
The school itself confirms the address: Surrey Schools' Cedar Hills page lists 12370 98 Avenue, Surrey, postal code V3V 2K3, and names the school Cedar Hills Elementary.

blocks.text: Cedar Hills Houses: the housing stock

items.t: The house stock is an established north-Surrey detached pattern around a long-standing elementary school, not a named new subdivision.

What can be stated from the district record is the school's scale in the system: Cedar Hills Elementary appears as site 73 in School District 36's 2026–2027 school listing, a Kindergarten to Grade 7 school serving the houses around 98 Avenue and 124 Street.

blocks.text: Cedar Hills Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The zoning check that matters is the lot's zone in Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, read lot by lot. Surrey replaced its old single-family zones in the July 8, 2024 rewrite: most former Single Family Residential (RF) lots are now R3 Urban Residential, intended for small-scale multi-unit housing on urban lots typically 560 square metres or larger, holding 2 to 6 dwelling units depending on lot size and location.

Subdivision minimums in R3 are a lot area of 560 square metres and a lot width of 15 metres, so an older Cedar Hills lot's split potential turns on whether it clears both figures — measure the surveyed lot, not the assessed frontage.

A houseplex (three or four units in one house-form building) is not a right on every lot: Surrey limits that form to the R3 zone on a lot with rear lane access or two street frontages, and a secondary suite is not permitted inside a houseplex.

blocks.text: Cedar Hills Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The district runs Kindergarten to Grade 7 elementary schools and Grade 8 to 12 secondary schools, with no middle-school tier. Surrey Schools states that structure directly, which matters for a Cedar Hills family planning a single elementary run at Cedar Hills Elementary followed by one secondary move.

Summer Learning runs at named sites, not at every school: the district's Summer Learning list includes Bridgeview Elementary at 12834 115A Avenue and Panorama Park Elementary at 12878 62 Avenue among its elementary sites — Cedar Hills Elementary is not listed as a Summer Learning site on that page.

blocks.text: Cedar Hills Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: The Cedar Hills-relevant cost is the suite charge: the City's 2026 tax brochure material records that properties with additional units are billed an $893.00 per-suite service fee in 2026, so a Cedar Hills house with a basement suite carries that yearly fee on top of the tax rate.
The Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) applies here because the City of Surrey is a designated taxable area, so every residential owner places the yearly declaration.
Cedar Hills' transit position is a bus-and-transfer position, not a station position.

The Surrey–Langley SkyTrain extension does not serve Cedar Hills: the Province states the extension runs from King George Station to Langley City Centre along Fraser Highway, on the opposite side of Surrey from 98 Avenue.

blocks.text: Cedar Hills Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: The first due-diligence step here is identity, not hazards: confirm which Cedar Hills the listing means. The verified school anchor is at 12370 98 Avenue in north Surrey; material online that pairs "Cedar Hills" with Newton schools around 66 Avenue describes different ground and must not be used for a 98 Avenue house.

Check the lot's zone, lane access and Frequent Bus Stop Area status in the City's COSMOS map before pricing in extra units: the difference between 3, 4 and 6 permitted units turns on lot area (280 square metres) and that mapped overlay, and a houseplex additionally needs lane or dual frontage.

blocks.text: Cedar Hills home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

57 houses sold in Cedar Hills with a median price of $1,100,000 (the middle half sold between $1,000,000 and $1,345,500), taking a median of 44 days to sell at 94.1% of the last list price; 5% sold above list. They had a median $445 per square foot, a median year built of 1964 and a median lot of 7,560 square feet.

faq.a: Cedar Hills Elementary is the named in-area school, at 12370 98 Avenue, Kindergarten to Grade 7. Surrey Schools lists that address on the school's own page, and the provincial school list confirms the grade range — but catchment is set by the exact home address, so run the address in the district's School Locator before treating any one house as in-catchment.
faq.q: Which elementary school serves a Cedar Hills house?

faq.a: Earlier area research paired the Cedar Hills name with Tamanawis Secondary, but Tamanawis is at 12600 66 Avenue — far south in Newton — while Cedar Hills Elementary is at 98 Avenue in north Surrey, so that pairing is not repeated here; confirm the secondary catchment for the specific address in the School District 36 locator.
faq.q: Which secondary school will my child attend?

faq.a: It depends on the zone and the lot, not on the Cedar Hills name. Under Surrey's small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) rules as written into Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, an eligible R3 lot under 280 square metres is capped at 3 units, a larger eligible lot at 4, and a lot of at least 281 square metres inside a Frequent Bus Stop Area at up to 6 — setbacks, parking and lane access still decide what actually fits.
faq.q: How many homes can go on my lot now?

faq.a: Catchment is address-based and capacity can override it. Surrey Schools states that your catchment school is determined by your address on the district's School Boundaries Map, that the School Locator returns it, and that Grade 7 students in a district elementary school are registered into their feeder secondary school automatically — enrolment at a school of choice still depends on availability.
faq.q: How does registration and catchment actually work in Surrey?
